chunks: From Abu Dharr (may Allah be pleased with him), he said:

I saw the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) strike the shoulder of Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him) with his hand and say: O Ali, whoever loves us is the Arab, and whoever hates us is the 'Ajj (non-Arab/foreigner). Our Shia are the people of the houses, the mines, and nobility, and whoever is born legitimate. And upon the religion of Abraham (peace be upon him) there is none but us and our Shia, and the rest of the people are free from it. Indeed, Allah and His angels destroy the evil deeds of our Shia just as people destroy a building.

key_terms.أَهْلُ الْبَيُوتَاتِ: People of the houses (referring to the Ahl al-Bayt)
key_terms.الْمَعَادِن: Mines (metaphor for sources of precious qualities or lineage)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of the Prophet striking Ali's shoulder in this hadith from Fadail al-Shia?
ai.summary: In Fadail al-Shia, Shaykh al-Saduq records this narration to establish the theological link between love for the Ahl al-Bayt and authentic Arab identity, contrasting it with the 'Ajj (in this specific context) with the 'Ajj (non-Arabs). The hadith emphasizes that the Shia are the true inheritors of Ibrahim's monotheism, distinguished by noble lineage and spiritual purity, with Allah and His angels erasing their sins as easily as one destroys a building.

en.badr-shahin: I saw the Prophet (s) strike on the shoulder of Ali bin Abi Talib (a) and say: O Ali, he who loves us is the true Arab and he who hates us is the infidel. Our Shia are the masters, the highborn, the honorable, and the legitimate. Only are our Shia and we following the religion of Abraham (a). The remaining people are all out of it -i.e. the religion of Abraham-. Allah and His angels are surely destroying the evil deeds of our Shia in the same way as an axe destroys the building.
